messages:
sanjay: Billing alert — unexpected spike for the GPU fleet in us-east1 around 16:10 UTC. Noticed ~12x cost on one line item. Anyone touching autoscaler or templates?
infra-bot: [ALERT] cost-anomaly detected for project:redwood-inference — +$18k over 1h vs baseline. Resource: compute.instances, zone: us-east1-b.
billing-bot: Line items: 12 x n2-highmem-32 (on-demand) from 16:05-16:35. Estimated extra cost: $17,600.
maria: Uhh — our GPU pool should be a100s (gpu-pool-a100) preemptible. Why n2-highmem?
sanjay: Running quick check: `gcloud compute instances list --filter="creationTimestamp>2026-03-18T16:00:00Z" --zones=us-east1-b` 

```
NAME                         ZONE        MACHINE_TYPE      PREEMPTIBLE  STATUS
autoscale-node-20260318-1    us-east1-b  n2-highmem-32     FALSE        RUNNING
autoscale-node-20260318-2    us-east1-b  n2-highmem-32     FALSE        RUNNING
gpu-node-a100-1              us-east1-c  a2-highgpu-1g     TRUE         RUNNING
```

maria: The autoscaler probably matched a node pool with wrong instance template. There was a terraform change to autoscaler recently?
alex: I just merged infra/terraform#412 yesterday — I added a fallback target pool for region-level scaling to avoid capacity constraints. Probably accidentally allowed us-east1-b to use the generic compute template. Sorry, that PR loosened the `node_pool` selector.
jen: Can you paste the snippet? I recall a var switch: `allowed_instance_types = var.fallback_types` and fallback_types included n2-highmem-*.
alex: Yep snippet from merged commit: 

```
module "gpu_autoscaler" {
  source = "./modules/autoscaler"
  node_selector = var.node_selector // previously strict label, now region-based
  allowed_instance_types = var.fallback_types // includes n2-highmem-32 for fallback
}
```

maria: So autoscaler policy fell back to a non-GPU template because zone capacity for GPUs was low — but we should never launch non-GPU nodes into the GPU tainted pool. That's the real misconfig.
sanjay: For immediate mitigation: I disabled the fallback in TF state by applying a quick patch: set `allowed_instance_types = []` for gpu_autoscaler and ran `terraform apply` at 16:20. Confirmed new nodes stopped launching.
jen: Good. We should also evict and delete the accidental n2 nodes and move workloads off them. Any jobs scheduled there?
maria: Two training jobs mistakenly picked them up — I drained both nodes: `kubectl drain autoscale-node-20260318-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `gcloud compute instances delete autoscale-node-20260318-1 --zone=us-east1-b -q`
sanjay: Deleted both by 16:33. Billing line items still show the charges until end of hour.
billing-bot: FYI: cloud provider billing reflects instance runtime; deletion prevents further accrual but doesn't refund prior hour usage.
alex: Action items I propose: 1) revert the loose node_selector change in infra/terraform#412 (PR queued), 2) add an explicit taint-check assertion in the autoscaler so it never matches non-gpu templates to gpu pools, 3) add cost guardrails to block non-gpu machine types from being created in gpu node pool.
jen: Also let's add an alert: if autoscaler creates >2 non-gpu nodes tagged with gpu-pool label in 30m, fire a P0.
maria: I'll file an incident postmortem — include cost impact, root cause (fallback_types + region fallback), and go-forward policy. Assigning to @alex for the rollback and @sanjay for immediate remediation notes.
sanjay: Quick note — we saw autoscaler TTL for fallback set to 0 in the module which caused immediate fallback launching rather than a cooldown. I added cooldown 10m in the hotfix.
alex: PR posted: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/419 — reintroduce strict node_selector and remove fallback_types from gpu_autoscaler.
jen: TL;DR: misconfiguration allowed region fallback to match non-gpu template -> autoscaler launched expensive on-demand n2 nodes into gpu pool -> cost spike. Remediation done, follow-up postmortem + policy changes.
maria: I'll create the postmortem doc and link billing export. Also scheduling a 30m retro with infra + billing.
sanjay: Thanks everyone. Please add any other notes in the incident doc. :thumbsup:
